claim: A set of diverse benchmark datasets is essential for identifying biases when they do arise.
source: Furthermore, a set of diverse benchmark datasets is essential for identifying such biases when they do arise.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the results.

claim: Neurons in CEM500K-moco models had consistently stronger invariance to all tested transformations compared to IN-moco models, with two exceptions.
source: We observed that neurons in CEM500K-moco models had consistently stronger invariance to all tested transformations (Figure 3a). The two exceptions were a reduction in invariance when contrast was very high and a smaller reduction when scale factors were very large (Figure 3a,v and vi, respectively).
evidence: This is a result from the invariance analysis.

claim: Virtually all the neurons in the CEM500K-moco model were remarkably invariant to rotation compared to about 70% of the neurons in the IN-moco model.
source: First, with regard to rotation, virtually all the neurons in the CEM500K-moco model were remarkably invariant to rotation compared to about 70% of the neurons in the IN-moco model, reflecting the fact that orientation matters for representing images in ImageNet but, appropriately, not for CEM500K.
evidence: This is a result from the rotation invariance analysis.

claim: Neurons in the CEM500K-moco model fire more consistently when presented with increasingly blurry and noisy images compared to IN-moco.
source: Next, neurons in the CEM500K-moco model fire more consistently when presented with increasingly blurry and noisy images, in both cases falling off significantly later as compared to IN-moco, when, presumably, meaningful information in the images has been lost.
evidence: This is a result from the blur and noise invariance analysis.

claim: The CEM500K-moco model had a noticeably greater invariance to both more brightened and more darkened images compared to IN-moco.
source: Further, while both of the tested pre-trained models responded comparably to increasing image brightness, the CEM500K-moco model had a noticeably greater invariance to both more brightened and more darkened images.
evidence: This is a result from the brightness invariance analysis.

claim: Very low-contrast images are common in CEM500K and cellular EM data more broadly, while very high-contrast images are not.
source: This was indicative of the distribution of images in CEM500K, and cellular EM data more broadly: very low-contrast images are common, very high-contrast images are not.
evidence: This is an observation about the characteristics of EM data.

claim: Heatmaps from the CEM500K-moco model shared a higher correlation with the presence of an organelle than features from the equivalent IN-moco model for ER, mitochondria, and nucleus.
source: We observed that these derived heatmaps from the CEM500K-moco model shared a higher correlation with the presence of an organelle than features from the equivalent IN-moco model, irrespective of whether the organelle interrogated was ER, mitochondria, or nucleus.
evidence: This is a result from the feature selectivity analysis.

claim: For the CEM500K-moco model, Point-Biserial correlation coefficients were 0.418, 0.680, and 0.888 for ER, mitochondria, and nucleus.
source: For the CEM500K-moco model, Point-Biserial correlation coefficients were 0.418, 0.680, and 0.888 for ER, mitochondria, and nucleus compared to 0.329, 0.608, and 0.803 for the IN-moco model.
evidence: This is a measured correlation coefficient.

claim: For the IN-moco model, Point-Biserial correlation coefficients were 0.329, 0.608, and 0.803 for ER, mitochondria, and nucleus.
source: For the CEM500K-moco model, Point-Biserial correlation coefficients were 0.418, 0.680, and 0.888 for ER, mitochondria, and nucleus compared to 0.329, 0.608, and 0.803 for the IN-moco model.
evidence: This is a measured correlation coefficient.

claim: The segmentations created by binarizing the mean responses have a greater IoU with ground truth segmentations for CEM500K-moco (0.284, 0.517, and 0.887 for ER, mitochondria, and nucleus) compared to IN-moco (0.208, 0.325, and 0.790).
source: The segmentations created by binarizing the mean responses also have a greater IoU with ground truth segmentations (CEM500K-moco: 0.284, 0.517, and 0.887 for ER, mitochondria, and nucleus; IN-moco: 0.208, 0.325, and 0.790, respectively) for the model.
evidence: This is a measured IoU score.

claim: Features learned from ImageNet displayed some selectivity for mitochondria and nuclei.
source: Unexpectedly, features learned from ImageNet displayed some selectivity for mitochondria and nuclei, emphasizing the surprising transferability of features to domains that are seemingly unrelated to a model's training dataset.
evidence: This is an observation from the feature selectivity analysis.

claim: Occlusion analysis showed that the model spontaneously learned to use organelles as 'landmarks' in the images without any guidance.
source: Results are displayed as heatmaps overlaid on the occluded image (Figure 3c) and show, importantly, that without any guidance the model spontaneously learned to use organelles as 'landmarks' in the images, visible as 'hot spots' around such features.
evidence: This is a result from the occlusion analysis.

claim: Sample preparation protocols for electron microscopy are explicitly designed to accentuate organelles and membranes relative to other content.
source: That these prominent objects should happen to be organelles is not coincidental as sample preparation protocols for electron microscopy are explicitly designed to accentuate organelles and membranes relative to other content.
evidence: This is a statement about EM sample preparation.

claim: CEM500K-moco was the best initialization method across all benchmarks with performance increases over random initialization ranging from 0.2% on the Lucchi++ benchmark to 73% on UroCell.
source: Across the board, CEM500K-moco was the best initialization method with performance increases over random initialization ranging from 0.2% on the Lucchi++ benchmark to a massive 73% on UroCell; the mean improvement (excluding CREMI Synaptic Clefts) was 30%.
evidence: This is a key result from the benchmark evaluation.

claim: The mean improvement of CEM500K-moco over random initialization (excluding CREMI Synaptic Clefts) was 30%.
source: Across the board, CEM500K-moco was the best initialization method with performance increases over random initialization ranging from 0.2% on the Lucchi++ benchmark to a massive 73% on UroCell; the mean improvement (excluding CREMI Synaptic Clefts) was 30%.
evidence: This is a measured performance improvement.

claim: On average, IN-super and IN-moco achieved 11% and 14% higher IoU scores than random initialization, respectively.
source: On average, IN-super and IN-moco achieved 11% and 14% higher IoU scores than random initialization, respectively.
evidence: This is a measured performance improvement.

claim: Parameters pre-trained with the unsupervised MoCoV2 algorithm transfer better to new tasks than parameters pre-trained on the ImageNet supervised classification task.
source: Parameters pre-trained with the unsupervised MoCoV2 algorithm thus appear to transfer better to new tasks than parameters pre-trained on the ImageNet supervised classification task (He et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the results, supported by a citation.

claim: The 14% average increase in IoU scores from CEM500K-moco over IN-moco reveals the advantage of pre-training on a domain-specific dataset.
source: Crucially, the 14% average increase in IoU scores from CEM500K-moco over IN-moco reveals the advantage of pre-training on a domain-specific dataset.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the results.

claim: Models pre-trained with the MoCoV2 algorithm converged the fastest.
source: We found that models pre-trained with the MoCoV2 algorithm converged the fastest (Figure 4d, top).
evidence: This is a result from the convergence analysis.

claim: Within just 500 iterations, MoCoV2 pre-trained models reach over 90% of their performance at 10,000 training iterations.
source: Within just 500 iterations, these models reach over 90% of their performance at 10,000 training iterations, and within only 100 iterations, they achieve over 80%.
evidence: This is a result from the convergence analysis.

claim: Within only 100 iterations, MoCoV2 pre-trained models achieve over 80% of their performance at 10,000 training iterations.
source: Within just 500 iterations, these models reach over 90% of their performance at 10,000 training iterations, and within only 100 iterations, they achieve over 80%.
evidence: This is a result from the convergence analysis.

claim: In some cases, 100 iterations required less than 45 s of training on the authors' hardware, which included an Nvidia P100 GPU.
source: In some cases, 100 iterations required less than 45 s of training on our hardware, which included an Nvidia P100 GPU, making this approach more feasible for resource-limited work.
evidence: This is a measured training time.

claim: The faster training associated with the MoCoV2 algorithm stems from the much lower magnitudes of feature activations, which facilitates training with higher learning rates.
source: We posit that the faster training associated with the MoCoV2 algorithm stems from the much lower magnitudes of feature activations, as observed in Tian et al., 2019, which facilitates training with higher learning rates.
evidence: This is an inference about why MoCoV2 trains faster, supported by a citation.

claim: The performance of randomly initialized models leveled off after 5000 iterations.
source: Finally, the plot of average IoU scores over a range of training iterations showed that the performance of randomly initialized models leveled off after 5000 iterations, see Figure 4d, bottom.
evidence: This is a result from the training iteration analysis.

claim: After 30,000 iterations of training on the easiest benchmarks (Perez, Lucchi++, and Kasthuri++), the performance of randomly initialized models effectively reached parity with CEM500K-moco models.
source: Previously, it has been observed that granted enough time to converge, randomly initialized models can often achieve comparable results to pre-trained models (He et al., 2018), and we did observe this for the easiest benchmarks (Perez, Lucchi++, and Kasthuri++, data not shown). After 30,000 iterations of training on these benchmarks, the performance of randomly initialized models effectively reached parity with CEM500K-moco models.
evidence: This is a result from extended training experiments, supported by a citation.

claim: For the hard benchmarks, randomly initialized models never reached the average IoU scores measured at even just 500 training iterations for CEM500K-moco models.
source: However, for the hard benchmarks, randomly initialized models never reached the average IoU scores measured at even just 500 training iterations for CEM500K-moco models.
evidence: This is a result from the training iteration analysis.

claim: CEM500K-moco pre-trained models outperformed the customized algorithms and training schemes presented as baselines for four of the benchmarks tested (by 3.0% on Guay, 8.6% on Kasthuri++, 1.2% on Lucchi++, and 10% on Perez).
source: Indeed, these models outperformed the customized algorithms and training schemes presented as baselines for four of the benchmarks that we tested (by 3.0% on Guay, 8.6% on Kasthuri++, 1.2% on Lucchi++, and 10% on Perez), see Table 2.
evidence: This is a comparison with previously published results.

claim: CEM500K is a diverse, relevant, information-rich, and non-redundant dataset of unlabeled cellular EM images designed to aid in the development of more robust and general DL models.
source: CEM500K is a diverse, relevant, information-rich, and non-redundant dataset of unlabeled cellular EM images designed expressly to aid in the development of more robust and general DL models.
evidence: This is a summary statement about CEM500K.

claim: CEM500K is derived from a far greater variety of tissue types, experimental conditions, and imaging techniques than other larger, publicly available EM datasets.
source: Above all, two features distinguish CEM500K from other larger, publicly available EM datasets that make it superior for DL applications. First, it is derived from a far greater variety of tissue types, experimental conditions, and imaging techniques, resulting in models with less bias toward such specific variables.
evidence: This is a comparison with other datasets.

claim: CEM500K is condensed by aggressively deleting redundant and uninformative images, which improves model performance and renders CEM500K more accessible to users.
source: Second, it is condensed by aggressively deleting redundant and uninformative images; this improves model performance and renders CEM500K more accessible to users.
evidence: This describes a key feature of CEM500K.

claim: Models pre-trained on CEM500K performed better on average than those pre-trained on a dataset extracted from a single large EM volume (Bloss) when evaluated on seven benchmarks.
source: By evaluating on seven benchmarks that represent different segmentation tasks and biological contexts, we demonstrate that, on average, models pre-trained on CEM500K performed better than those pre-trained on a dataset extracted from a single large EM volume (Bloss).
evidence: This is a key result of the study.

claim: The targeted removal of 90% of the images from the original corpus of data to generate CEM500K returned a significant increase in the quality of pre-trained parameters as measured by segmentation IoU scores.
source: Remarkably, the targeted removal of 90% of the images from the original corpus of data to generate CEM500K returned a significant increase in the quality of pre-trained parameters as measured by segmentation IoU scores.
evidence: This is a key finding about the value of curation.

claim: Pre-training exclusively on images of mouse brain tissue (Bloss) did not improve performance over CEM500K on benchmarks from that same tissue.
source: Pre-training exclusively on images of mouse brain tissue (Bloss) did not improve performance over CEM500K on benchmarks from that same tissue (see Figure 2e).
evidence: This is a result from the comparison with the Bloss dataset.

claim: As dataset size decreases, it becomes more likely that a model will overfit to the pre-training task and learn image features that are irrelevant for other downstream tasks.
source: Further, we speculate that as dataset size decreases, it becomes more likely that a model will overfit to the pre-training task and learn image features that are irrelevant for other downstream tasks (Tian and Sun, 2020; Minderer et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by citations.

claim: Parameters trained on CEM500K are a strong and general-purpose starting point for improving downstream segmentation models.
source: Regardless, we have shown here that parameters trained on CEM500K are a strong and general-purpose starting point for improving downstream segmentation models.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study.

claim: U-Nets pre-trained on CEM500K significantly outperformed randomly initialized U-Nets on all of the segmentation benchmarks tested, with the largest improvements corresponding to the most difficult benchmarks.
source: U-Nets pre-trained on CEM500K significantly outperformed randomly initialized U-Nets on all of the segmentation benchmarks that we tested, with the largest improvements corresponding to the most difficult benchmarks.
evidence: This is a key result of the study.

claim: CEM500K pre-trained models achieved state-of-the-art IoU scores on all benchmarks for which comparison with previous results was possible.
source: Impressively, such pre-trained models achieved state-of-the-art IoU scores on all benchmarks for which comparison with previous results was possible.
evidence: This is a key result of the study.

claim: Pre-trained parameters have been shown to guide downstream models to converge to more general optima than they would from random initialization.
source: In general, pre-trained parameters have been shown to guide downstream models to converge to more general optima than they would from random initialization (Huh et al., 2016; Yosinski et al., 2014; Neyshabur et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: As the number of examples in the training dataset increases, the generalization benefits from transfer learning start to diminish (gains in training speed are retained).
source: As the number of examples in the training dataset increases the generalization benefits from transfer learning start to diminish (gains in training speed are retained)(Zoph, 2020; He et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Using CEM500K as seed data provides a path forward for creating general segmentation models that reliably segment features of interest for data generated by novel experiments.
source: However, using CEM500K as seed data provides a path forward for tackling this much more difficult challenge.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential future use of CEM500K.

claim: CEM500K is the most comprehensive and diversified resource of cellular EM images to the authors' knowledge.
source: With 0.5 × 106 uniquely informative images representing approximately six hundred 3D and ten thousand 2D images corresponding to more than 100 completely unrelated biological projects, CEM500K is to our knowledge the most comprehensive and diversified resource of cellular EM images.
evidence: This is a claim about the uniqueness of CEM500K.

claim: Annotating images from CEM500K will enable the creation of new task-specific training datasets with substantially more variety than previously available.
source: Annotating images from CEM500K (or identifying them as negative examples) will enable the creation of new task-specific training datasets with substantially more variety than previously available.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential future use of CEM500K.

claim: Models trained on datasets created by annotating CEM500K images will likely be better equipped to handle data from new microscopes, biological contexts, and sample preparation protocols.
source: Models trained on such datasets will likely be better equipped to handle data from new microscopes, biological contexts, and sample preparation protocols.
evidence: This is a speculation about future models.

claim: Each image chosen for annotation from CEM500K is likely to be uniquely informative for a model because of the extensive deduplication and filtering pipeline.
source: Moreover, each image chosen for annotation from CEM500K is likely to be uniquely informative for a model because of the extensive deduplication and filtering pipeline that we have created and used here, and which we share for future work by the community.
evidence: This is an inference about the value of images in CEM500K.

claim: All but one of the available benchmarks involved the annotation of mitochondria.
source: In particular, all but one of the benchmarks involved the annotation of mitochondria and three of the seven were from mouse brain tissue.
evidence: This is an observation about the benchmark datasets.

claim: Three of the seven benchmarks were from mouse brain tissue.
source: In particular, all but one of the benchmarks involved the annotation of mitochondria and three of the seven were from mouse brain tissue.
evidence: This is an observation about the benchmark datasets.

claim: Benchmark variety is essential to identify biases in pre-trained parameters.
source: We observed that benchmark variety is essential to identify biases in pre-trained parameters and that difficult tasks are a necessary and stringent test of pre-training algorithms or datasets.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the results.

claim: Difficult tasks are a necessary and stringent test of pre-training algorithms or datasets.
source: We observed that benchmark variety is essential to identify biases in pre-trained parameters and that difficult tasks are a necessary and stringent test of pre-training algorithms or datasets.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the results.

claim: The authors only tested semantic and not instance segmentation.
source: Additionally, we only tested semantic and not instance segmentation (i.e. all objects from one class share one label).
evidence: This describes a limitation of the study.

claim: The authors made the decision to focus on semantic segmentation in order to avoid the more complex model architectures, postprocessing, and hyperparameters that usually accompany instance segmentation.
source: We made this decision in order to avoid the more complex model architectures, postprocessing, and hyperparameters that usually accompany instance segmentation (Heinrich et al., 2018; Funke et al., 2019; Januszewski et al., 2018).
evidence: This explains the rationale for focusing on semantic segmentation, supported by citations.

claim: 2D models work well for semantic segmentation in both 2D and 3D.
source: 2D models work well for semantic segmentation in both 2D and 3D (our 2D models beat the state-of-the-art results set by 3D models on some of the benchmarks, see Table 2) and from a computational standpoint, running training and inference on 2D data typically requires fewer resources.
evidence: This is a statement about the effectiveness of 2D models.

claim: The authors' 2D models beat the state-of-the-art results set by 3D models on some of the benchmarks.
source: 2D models work well for semantic segmentation in both 2D and 3D (our 2D models beat the state-of-the-art results set by 3D models on some of the benchmarks, see Table 2) and from a computational standpoint, running training and inference on 2D data typically requires fewer resources.
evidence: This is a result from the benchmark evaluation.

claim: 2D pre-trained parameters are broadly useful for cellular EM researchers, especially for laboratories with limited access to high-performance computing.
source: Therefore, we believe that 2D pre-trained parameters are broadly useful for cellular EM researchers, especially for laboratories with limited access to high-performance computing.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of 2D pre-trained parameters.

claim: For some complex tasks like 3D instance segmentation, 2D models may perform poorly.
source: For some complex tasks like 3D instance segmentation, an important and common task in cellular EM connectomics research, 2D models may perform poorly.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of 2D models.

claim: Unsupervised pre-training on 3D data is currently an underexplored research area.
source: Unsupervised pre-training on 3D data is currently an underexplored research area and algorithms like MoCoV2 should work for pre-training 3D models.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of research.

claim: Algorithms like MoCoV2 should work for pre-training 3D models.
source: Unsupervised pre-training on 3D data is currently an underexplored research area and algorithms like MoCoV2 should work for pre-training 3D models.
evidence: This is a speculation about the applicability of MoCoV2 to 3D data.

claim: The creation of a 3D image dataset similar to CEM500K is likely to be of great use to the nascent volume EM community.
source: The creation of a 3D image dataset similar to the resource reported here is likely to be of great use to the nascent volume EM community.
evidence: This is a speculation about future work.

claim: The goal of this work is to begin the process of creating a data ecosystem for cellular EM images and datasets.
source: The goal of this work is to begin the process of creating a data ecosystem for cellular EM images and datasets.
evidence: This is a statement about the goal of the work.

claim: CEM500K will be a valuable resource for experimenting with and taking advantage of the latest developments in DL research.
source: CEM500K will be a valuable resource for experimenting with and taking advantage of the latest developments in DL research, where access to troves of image data is usually taken for granted.
evidence: This is a statement about the value of CEM500K.

claim: To further increase the utility of CEM500K, more data from uncommon organisms, tissue and cell types, sample preparation protocols, and acquisition parameters will be needed.
source: To further increase its utility, more data from uncommon organisms, tissue and cell types, sample preparation protocols, and acquisition parameters will be needed.
evidence: This is a statement about future improvements to CEM500K.

claim: In the current state, CEM500K is still heavily skewed to a few common organisms like mice and tissues like brain.
source: In the current state, the dataset is still heavily skewed to a few common organisms like mice and tissues like brain, and it is clear that there is much room for greater sampling and heterogeneity (Appendix 1—figure 6).
evidence: This is an observation about the current composition of CEM500K.

claim: The dataset has been made available for download on EMPIAR (ID 10592).
source: The dataset has been made available for download on EMPIAR (ID 10592).
evidence: This is a statement about data availability.

claim: The massive reduction in dataset size from curation makes the sharing of data relatively quick and easy.
source: The massive reduction in dataset size from curation makes the sharing of data relatively quick and easy; moreover, the elimination of 3D context from volume EM datasets ensures that the shared data can only reasonably be used for DL applications.

claim: The elimination of 3D context from volume EM datasets ensures that the shared data can only reasonably be used for DL applications.
source: The massive reduction in dataset size from curation makes the sharing of data relatively quick and easy; moreover, the elimination of 3D context from volume EM datasets ensures that the shared data can only reasonably be used for DL applications.
evidence: This is a statement about the implications of the curation process.

claim: The quality of the pre-trained parameters for transfer learning will improve logarithmically as CEM500K grows.
source: Similar to pre-training on natural images, we expect that the quality of the pre-trained parameters for transfer learning will improve logarithmically as CEM500K grows (Mahajan, 2018).
evidence: This is a speculation about future improvements, supported by a citation.

claim: Datasets generated from microscopes in the authors' lab were already in the desired standardized format: 8-bit unsigned volumes or 2D tiff images.
source: Datasets generated from microscopes in our lab were already in the desired standardized format: 8-bit unsigned volumes or 2D tiff images.
evidence: This describes the format of in-house data.

claim: To reduce the memory requirements of large 3D volumes, datasets were downsampled such that no individual dataset was larger than 5 GB (affecting only seven of the total 591 image volumes).
source: To reduce the memory requirements of large 3D volumes, datasets were downsampled such that no individual dataset was larger than 5 GB (affecting only seven of the total 591 image volumes).
evidence: This describes a preprocessing step.

claim: For all isotropic voxel data and for any anisotropic voxel data in which the z resolution was less than 20% different from the x and y resolutions, 2D cross-sections from the xy, xz, and yz planes were sequentially extracted.
source: For all isotropic voxel data and for any anisotropic voxel data in which the z resolution was less than 20% different from the x and y resolutions, 2D cross-sections from the xy, xz, and yz planes were sequentially extracted.
evidence: This describes a preprocessing step.

claim: Anisotropic voxel data with a greater than 20% difference in axial versus lateral resolutions were only sliced into cross-sections in the xy plane.
source: Anisotropic voxel data with a greater than 20% difference in axial versus lateral resolutions were only sliced into cross-sections in the xy plane.
evidence: This describes a preprocessing step.

claim: Images were cropped into 224 × 224 patches without any overlap.
source: These images were cropped into 224 × 224 patches without any overlap.
evidence: This describes a preprocessing step.

claim: If the image's width or height was not a multiple of 224, then crops from the remaining area were discarded if either of their dimensions were less than 112.
source: If the image's width or height was not a multiple of 224, then crops from the remaining area were discarded if either of their dimensions were less than 112.
evidence: This describes a preprocessing step.

claim: Cloud Volume API was used to randomly sample 1000 2D patches from the xy planes of each available dataset from the Open Connectome Project.
source: As these volumes were too large to reasonably download and store (tens of TB), Cloud Volume API was used to randomly sample 1000 2D patches from the xy planes of each available dataset.
evidence: This describes a data collection method.

claim: The 'Bloss baseline' dataset was extracted and generated with the Cloud Volume API method, with 1 × 10^6 patches collected from that single data volume to roughly match the number of images in CEMraw.
source: The 'Bloss baseline' dataset (Bloss et al., 2018) was also extracted and generated with this method; however, 1 × 106 patches were collected from that single data volume to roughly match the number of images in CEMraw (Appendix 1—figure 4).
evidence: This describes the creation of the Bloss baseline dataset.

claim: Difference hashes gave the best results of all the hashing algorithms tested for deduplication.
source: Difference hashes gave the best results of all the hashing algorithms tested (Kind of Like That, 2013).
evidence: This describes the choice of hashing algorithm.

claim: A hash size of 8 results in a 64-bit array to encode each 224 × 224 image.
source: A hash size of 8 results in a 64-bit array to encode each 224 × 224 image.
evidence: This describes the hashing parameters.

claim: Sets of hashes with a distance <12 between them were considered a group of near-duplicates.
source: Sets of hashes with a distance <12 (distance cutoff chosen by visual inspection of groups) between them were considered a group of near-duplicates.
evidence: This describes the deduplication threshold.

claim: A random subset of 14,000 images from CEMdedup were manually labeled either informative or uninformative.
source: A random subset of 14,000 images from CEMdedup were manually labeled either informative or uninformative.
evidence: This describes the manual labeling process.

claim: Images with 80% or more of their area occupied by uniform intensity structures like nuclei, cytoplasm, or resin are classified as uninformative.
source: Concretely, this means that images with 80% or more of their area occupied by uniform intensity structures like nuclei, cytoplasm, or resin are classified as uninformative.
evidence: This describes the criteria for uninformative images.

claim: 2000 labeled images were set aside as a test set and the remaining 12,000 were used as training data for a model classifier.
source: 2000 labeled images were set aside as a test set and the remaining 12,000 were used as training data for a model classifier: a ResNet34 pre-trained on ImageNet.

source: The fourth layer of residual blocks and the classification head of the model were fine-tuned for 30 epochs on a P100 GPU with the Adam optimizer and a learning rate of 0.001.

claim: Pre-training was completed on a machine with four Nvidia V100 GPUs using a batch size of 128 and queue length of 65,536.
source: Pre-training was completed on a machine with four Nvidia V100 GPUs using a batch size of 128 and queue length of 65,536.
evidence: This describes the hardware and hyperparameters for pre-training.

claim: The initial learning rate for MoCoV2 pre-training was set to 0.015 and divided by 10 at epochs 120 and 160.
source: The initial learning rate was set to 0.015 and divided by 10 at epochs 120 and 160.
evidence: This describes the learning rate schedule for pre-training.

claim: 360° rotations and Gaussian noise with a standard deviation range of 1 × 10^-5 to 1 × 10^-4 were added to the data augmentations for MoCoV2 pre-training.
source: In addition, 360° rotations and Gaussian noise with a standard deviation range of 1 × 10−5 to 1 × 10−4 were added to the data augmentations.
evidence: This describes additional data augmentations used.

source: For pre-training comparisons between different EM datasets, that is the three subsets of CEM plus Bloss (Figure 2d,e), 4.5 × 105 total parameter updates (iterations) were run for each model, which is equivalent to 120 passes (epochs) through all the images in CEM500K.
evidence: This describes the training schedule for comparison experiments.

claim: The average training time for each pre-training model in the comparison experiments was 2.5 days.
source: The average training time for each of these models was 2.5 days.
evidence: This is a measured training time.

claim: The final pre-trained parameters generated for results shown in Figure 4b,c were trained on CEM500K for an additional 80 epochs: a total of 200 epochs and 4 days of training.
source: The final pre-trained parameters generated for results shown in Figure 4b,c were trained on CEM500K for an additional 80 epochs: a total of 200 epochs and 4 days of training.
evidence: This describes the training schedule for the final model.

claim: The One Cycle Policy and AdamW optimizer with maximum learning rate 0.003, weight decay 0.1, batch size 16, and (binary) cross-entropy loss were used for all benchmarks.
source: The One Cycle Policy and AdamW optimizer with maximum learning rate 0.003, weight decay 0.1, batch size 16, and (binary) cross-entropy loss were used for all benchmarks (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2017; Smith, 2018).
evidence: This describes the training parameters for benchmark evaluation.

claim: For the Guay and Urocell benchmarks, the cross-entropy loss was weighted by the prevalence of each class.
source: For the Guay and Urocell benchmarks, which required multiclass segmentation, the cross-entropy loss was weighted by the prevalence of each class; we observed that this yielded better IoU scores on the Guay validation dataset (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This describes a modification to the loss function for specific benchmarks.

claim: For the Perez datasets, the authors ignored areas in the predicted segmentations that did not coincide with a labeled instance in the ground truth because test images did not have labels for all instances of an object.
source: First, test images in the Perez datasets did not have labels for all instances of an object; for example, only one nucleus was labeled in an image containing two nuclei. To circumvent this problem, we ignored areas in the predicted segmentations that did not coincide with a labeled instance in the ground truth.

claim: The authors eliminated the last four downsampling operations in the ResNet50 for ER feature selectivity analysis such that the output feature map was only 2x smaller than the input.
source: For thin and small organelles like ER, the final feature maps were too coarse to accurately show the localization of responses. Therefore, we eliminated the last four downsampling operations such that the output feature map was only 2x smaller than the input.
evidence: This describes a modification to the architecture for feature selectivity analysis.

claim: The authors eliminated the last two downsampling operations for mitochondria feature selectivity analysis such that the output was 8x smaller than the input.
source: Following similar logic, we eliminated the last two downsampling operations for mitochondria and the last downsampling operation for nuclei – 8x and 16x smaller than the input images, respectively.
evidence: This describes a modification to the architecture for feature selectivity analysis.
